findings.why_not_priced: The published bar is stale. Zacks' 1.1% and the +1.2% EPS revision over 30 days have not moved since the card data, and Wells overrides its own card read to model +1.0%, which is anchoring on the FY guide. It is partly priced: the Kalshi strikes already hold about 0.3% (thin, roughly $1-3k of volume per strike), and buy-side card panels likely show the same slowdown. Most of the surprise is therefore against the published number, not the price. If the market fully held a ~0.6% comp, the Kalshi 0.5% strike would sit near 0.55 instead of 0.40, and the sell-side bar would have been cut.

premortem.other_way_reason: The stock rallies 6-10%. US comps print at or above 1% on the July 50%-off week, Stuffed Crust's return and share taken from Papa John's and a Pizza Hut in a sale process. Jordan keeps 'low single digits' with an upbeat Domino and Q4-to-date number. A de-rated stock (16x forward, -15% since August) with calls bid and shorts already covering re-rates, as Q2's premarket +6.5-8% on a comp miss showed the buyers are there.
premortem.question: Q2
premortem.evidence_already_had: Wells' QTD-stronger card read and +1.0% model; Census and BofA restaurant acceleration and a strong September; Google search y/y improving in Q3; the +2.1% reaction to a held guide in July; skew -10.5.

investment_decision.reason: The print turns on Q1 and Q2. Q1 likely comes in below the stale 1.1% sell-side bar, but at roughly what the only market quoting the line already holds (Kalshi ~0.3%), and this name bought a comp miss in July when the guide held. Q2, whether a new insider CEO trims 'low single digits' with H1 at +0.5%, is close to a coin flip: the FY arithmetic argues for a trim, while Wells' Q4-to-date card read, the Domino launch and a strong September consumer argue against. Q3 and Q4 come back at their priced answers. The findings sum to -0.30, inside any cost or noise band against a 6% implied move, so the sign does not carry a trade.
investment_decision.what_would_change_it: A Q4-to-date US comp number on the call. Above about 2% would make the guide safe and the long right; flat or negative with a guide trim would make the short right.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): DPZ bought a 0.5pt comp miss in Q2 2026 (+2.1%) when orders grew and the guide held, so the reaction function shrinks the Q1 finding: -0.8 to about -0.55.

Lesson 5 (narrow proxy against a broad series; documents beat inference): re-read the Wells sentence. Its card-data figure is not stated as DPZ-specific, and Wells reconciles it to +90bp of acceleration. Kept the more direct series (DPZ and pizza card data) above the broad Census and BofA restaurant acceleration, but the weaker proxy plus the netted counter-evidence takes Q1 to -0.4 and moves the central comp from +0.4% to +0.6% (print_vs_bar -0.7 to -0.5).
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the comp bar is disputed (Zacks 1.1%, other models 0.72-1.0%, Kalshi ~0.3%), so every finding stays capped small and p_up moves toward 50.

Lesson 7 (positioning): the negative sign runs against a call-bid skew (-10.5) I cannot argue is wrong, so Q1 goes -0.4 to -0.3 and Q2 -0.2 to -0.1. Short interest is 7.8% with 3.1 days to cover and falling, not crowded, so no further squeeze cut.
Lesson 2 (name the line; one-offs at a fraction): Q4's DPC Dash mark is filed as a one_off at a fraction (-0.1), unchanged.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number) and reading the set: Q1 and Q2 carry their counter-evidence net in the size. No two findings contradict each other, and none shares a fact.

Pessimism artefact: three of four findings lean negative, so I re-checked the positive evidence (Census, BofA September, Google Q3, Jubilant, DPG, share donors). It is sized in, and the net sum of -0.30 is near zero.

Scaled measurement: p_up 46 to 48 (lessons 1, 6 and 7 each toward 50, applied once). abs_move 6.0 to 6.5, because a guidance change on a new CEO's first call is likely and the hunters' sizes have run small (core table). expected_move goes from -0.48 to -0.26.
